newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NEGOTIATIONS BEGIN OVER PUBLIC SERVICE AGREEMENTS
Negotiations have begun over a new enterprise agreement for the 120,000 Commonwealth public servants.
The Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, has met Community and Public Sector Union officials in Melbourne.
The union wants undertakings from the Government about job security and improved wages and conditions in return for more public service reforms.
It's says Mr Reith's views are outdated and that he's ignored the amount of flexibility already shown by the Commonwealth workforce.
Mr Reith says today's discussion were sensible and he looks forward to continuing them in the new year.
He says the CPSU has given him a log of claims but hasn't made a specific wage demand.
UPSWING IN HOUSING MARKET
New figures from the Real Estate Institute show an increase in housing market confidence on the back of lower interest rates.
A survey shows rents on three bedroom houses and two bedroom units up in all cities and the overbuilding of the early 1990's eased.
The Institute's Jenny Allen says first home owners are being hit hard by HECS repayments, and compulsory superannuation, but are surviving with the help of lower interest rates.
She says the lower rates will also help cushion any rise in house prices.
FORMER BANK CHIEF IN BANKRUPTCY HEARING
Former State Bank of South Australia boss, Tim Marcus Clark, has told a bankruptcy hearing in Melbourne that he divested himself of a million dollars in shares in 1989 to avoid death duties.
He began divesting his assets in late 1989 just after a writ was issued suing the directors of failed New Zealand company Equiticorp for A$450 million dollars.
He told the hearing he put his shares in trust for his children because he was worried about the reintroduction of death duties.
The hearing then learnt Mr Clark's son in early 1991 signed over his income from the shares to his father.
At one point there was an angry clash between Mr Clark and his inquisitor Jim Delaney over the pedantic way Mr Clark was answering questions.
PYRMAID BUILDING SOCIETY SETTLEMENT
A six year legal battle by shareholders in the collapsed Pyramid Building Society has ended with about 10,000 Shareholders accepting a settlement.
The Court of Appeal recently ruled in favor of non-withdrawable shareholders allowing them to be treated the same as other creditors.
Today, the Supreme Court indicated that subject to its own approval, the 10,000 shareholders will receive between 45 cents and 65 cents in the dollar, depending on their legal status.
The total payout will be around A$45 million dollars.
While some matters still have to be settled, today's announcement marks the end of the battle by shareholders against the State Government and three building societies owned by the Pyramid group.
SHARP DISMISSES REPORTS ABOUT WATERFRONT REFORMS
Federal Transport Minister John Sharp has joined other senior Government figures in dismissing reports the Government would be prepared to send the army to the waterfront during the reform process.
Prime Minister, John Howard, and Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, have also rejected the reports.
Mr Sharp says the Government does not propose to put troops on the waterfront and has said all along reform can be achieved without resorting to use of the military.
WEST AUSTRALIAN MAN SAVED BY WALLABY
Firefighters in Western Australia say a man's life has been saved by what they're calling the "skippy alarm", after his house caught fire in Woorooloo early this morning.
Last night, 31 year old, Nigel Etherington picked up a young rock wallaby who's mother had been killed by a car on the Great Eastern Highway north east of Perth.
Mr Etherington left the joey in his bathroom overnight.
About six o'clock this morning, he was woken by the wallaby thumping on the bathroom wall, and discovered the house full of smoke from a fire in another bedroom.
Mr Etherington says the wallaby, which has since made it's way back into the bush, saved his life.
-- Reuter Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
